newsitem.title: BELGIUM: TENNIS-FEW CHEERS FOR MONAMI ON RETURN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FEW CHEERS FOR MONAMI ON RETURN.

text.p: Belgium's new tennis star Dominique van Roost, who shot to fame at the Australian Open where she received thundering applause and standing ovations, returned home on Friday without a cheering crowd in sight.
The slender player, ranked number 43 in the world, was barely known abroad before the Melbourne tournament but grabbed world headlines by beating world number two Arantxa Sanchez.
But only a handful of relatives showed up at Brussels airport to welcome home van Roost, who retired injured in her quarter-final match against American Mary Joe Fernandez.
Van Roost said her Australian experience had taught here she could beat other top players.
"I cannot say whether I can win a grand slam tournament but after the match I played against Sanchez, I know now that I have a good chance of beating any of the top players," van Roost told Reuters.
Van Roost, who injured an abdomen muscle at the Open, will now rest 10 days before returning to the game.
"My next match will be in Paris but whether I'll go will depend on my injuries," she said.
Van Roost who played only her first grand slam event in Australia, expected to improve her ranking to about 30th place.
She said her improved physical fitness had been the key to success, but added she would not change her game.
"For women's tennis what happened in the Australian Open was a revolution, with top players suffering first-round defeats," she said.
Van Roost and compatriot Sabine Appelmans were Belgium's first women ever to reach the quarter-final stage of a grand slam tournament.
